unit_label: Module B unit 2: climate risk and green deposits

facts.statement: Climate related risks are the potential risks that may arise from climate change or from efforts to mitigate it, their impact and the economic and financial consequences, and they reach the financial sector through two channels. Physical risks arise from changes in weather and climate that affect the economy: acute risks (floods, heatwaves, landslides and other extreme events) and chronic risks (gradual shifts such as ocean acidification, rising sea levels and extreme weather variability); their effect depends on geography, since some regions are more exposed and vulnerable; for banks the economic and financial effects include damage to property and infrastructure, business disruption, a fall in the value of property securing exposures and impaired ability of borrowers to perform. Transition risks arise from the adjustment to a low-carbon economy and can be grouped into mitigation policies (for example lower financial valuation or downgrades of business credit ratings, or subsidies to encourage energy efficient goods and processes), technological advances (which can speed the energy transition and the use of non-fossil fuels that reduce greenhouse gas emissions) and shifts in public sentiment among consumers and investors.

Under the Reserve Bank's Climate Finance and Management of Climate Change Risks Directions, 2025 (as read, a framework for green deposits), a green deposit is an interest-bearing deposit received for a fixed period whose proceeds are earmarked for green finance; green finance is lending to or investing in qualifying green activities or projects that contribute to climate risk mitigation, climate adaptation and resilience and other climate-related or environmental objectives including biodiversity management and nature-based solutions; greenwashing is marketing products or services as green when they do not meet the requirements. Raising green deposits is optional but a bank that does so must have a Board-approved policy on green deposits (published on its website) and a Board-approved Financing Framework. A bank may finance green projects irrespective of raising green deposits but may not finance a project first and raise green deposits for it afterwards. Green deposits are issued as cumulative or non-cumulative deposits, in Indian rupees only, with tenor, size, interest rate and terms as in the deposit interest rate Directions; differential interest on green deposits is not permitted, interest is paid whatever the allocation of proceeds, premature withdrawal is not restricted by this framework and does not affect the projects financed, the deposits are covered by DICGC insurance, and an overdraft against a green deposit is allowed under the credit risk management Directions.

The Financing Framework covers the eligible green activities, the process for project evaluation and selection, the allocation of proceeds and reporting, third-party verification and impact assessment, and the temporary allocation of unallocated proceeds, which may be held only in Level 1 high quality liquid assets with a maximum original tenor of one year; there is no penalty for non-allocation but it is subject to supervisory review. The framework must be reviewed externally and, with the reviewer's opinion, published on the bank's website before implementation. Proceeds are allocated according to the official Indian green taxonomy; pending its finalisation, to interim categories: renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation, climate change adaptation, sustainable water and waste management, pollution prevention and control, green buildings, sustainable management of living natural resources and land use, and terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity conservation. Excluded are fossil fuel extraction, production and distribution (or projects with a fossil-fuel core energy source), nuclear power, direct waste incineration, the alcohol, weapons, tobacco, gaming and palm oil industries, biomass energy using feedstock from protected areas, landfill projects and hydropower plants larger than 25 MW. The allocation in each financial year is subject to annual independent third-party verification or assurance, which does not absolve the bank of responsibility for end use; the bank also assesses the impact annually with external firms in an Impact Assessment Report using indicators such as renewable capacity, energy generated or saved and greenhouse gas emissions avoided in tonnes of CO2 equivalent; both reports are placed on the website, and a review report goes to the Board or its delegated committee within three months of the end of the financial year covering the amount raised, the projects financed and amounts allocated, and the two reports.

payload.title: Climate risk: physical and transition
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Climate related risk** = **potential risk from climate change or from efforts to limit it**, reaching banks through **two channels**.

| Channel | Types | Bank effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Physical risk** | **acute** (**floods, heatwaves, landslides**) and **chronic** (**sea level rise, ocean acidification, extreme weather variability**) | **damage to property and infrastructure; business disruption; fall in value of collateral; borrowers less able to repay**; **depends on geography** |
| **Transition risk** | **mitigation policies** (**lower valuations, rating downgrades, subsidies for efficiency**); **technological advances** (**non-fossil fuels**); **shifts in public sentiment** (**consumers and investors**) | **adjustment to a low-carbon economy affects the economy** |

payload.title: The green deposit framework: rules for the bank
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Definitions**: **green deposit** = **interest-bearing deposit for a fixed period whose proceeds are earmarked for green finance**; **green finance** = **lending to or investing in qualifying green activities or projects**; **greenwashing** = **marketing as green something that does not qualify**.

| Rule | Position |
| --- | --- |
| **Raising green deposits** | **optional**; if done, **Board-approved policy (on the website) and Financing Framework** |
| **Order** | **may finance green projects without raising green deposits**; **may not finance first and raise green deposits afterwards** |
| **Currency** | **Indian rupees only** |
| **Interest** | **no differential rate**; **paid whatever the allocation** |
| **Deposit insurance** | **covered by DICGC** |
| **Overdraft against it** | **allowed** under the credit risk management Directions |

payload.title: Use of proceeds, exclusions and assurance
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Parking proceeds**: **only in Level 1 HQLA with original tenor up to one year**. **No penalty for non-allocation, but supervisory review**.

**Eligible (interim, until the official Indian green taxonomy)**: **renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation, climate change adaptation, water and waste management, pollution control, green buildings, sustainable land use, biodiversity conservation**.

**Excluded**: **fossil fuels, nuclear power, direct waste incineration, alcohol, weapons, tobacco, gaming and palm oil, biomass from protected areas, landfills, hydropower above 25 MW**.

| Control | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| **Framework** | **external review; published with the reviewer's opinion before use** |
| **Third-party verification** | **annual, independent**; **does not remove the bank's end-use responsibility** |
| **Impact assessment** | **annual, with external firms**; indicators such as **energy saved and greenhouse gas emissions avoided** |
| **Reporting** | **both reports on the website**; **Board review report within three months of year end** |

payload.stem_md: Through which two broad channels can climate-related risks affect the financial sector?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Climate-related risks reach the financial sector through physical risks and transition risks.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is a chronic physical risk?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Chronic physical risks come from gradual shifts such as ocean acidification and rising sea levels; floods, heatwaves and landslides are acute.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is a driver of transition risk?

options.text_md: A shift in consumer and investor sentiment

payload.correct_explanation_md: Transition risk drivers include mitigation policies, technological advances and shifts in public sentiment.

payload.stem_md: How can physical climate risk impair a bank's loan book?

options.text_md: By reducing the value of property securing exposures and borrowers' ability to perform
By closing the bank's branches by law

payload.correct_explanation_md: Physical risks reflect damage to property, infrastructure and business, lowering collateral values and the ability of borrowers to repay.

payload.stem_md: How do the Directions define a green deposit?

options.text_md: A deposit that pays a higher rate than ordinary deposits
An interest-bearing deposit for a fixed period whose proceeds are earmarked for green finance
A deposit in a green coloured account

payload.correct_explanation_md: A green deposit is an interest-bearing deposit received for a fixed period, the proceeds of which are earmarked for allocation to green finance.

options.text_md: Marketing products or services as green when they do not meet the requirements

payload.correct_explanation_md: Greenwashing is marketing products or services as green when in fact they do not meet the requirements for green activities.

payload.stem_md: In which currency may green deposits be denominated?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Green deposits are denominated only in Indian rupees and not in any foreign currency.

payload.stem_md: May a bank pay a higher rate of interest on green deposits than on comparable ordinary deposits?

options.text_md: No, differential interest on green deposits is not permitted
Yes, if the project is solar

payload.correct_explanation_md: The extant guidelines do not permit a differential rate of interest on green deposits.

payload.stem_md: Are deposits raised under the green deposit framework covered by deposit insurance?

options.text_md: Yes, by DICGC in accordance with its Act and regulations

payload.correct_explanation_md: Deposits raised under the framework are covered by DICGC.

payload.stem_md: Which sequence is NOT allowed under the Directions?

options.text_md: Financing a green project without raising green deposits
Raising green deposits and then financing a project
Financing a green project first and then raising green deposits for it
Not raising green deposits at all

payload.correct_explanation_md: A bank cannot finance green activities first and raise green deposits thereafter for the same projects.

payload.stem_md: Pending allocation, in what may a bank temporarily park green deposit proceeds?

options.text_md: Level 1 HQLA with a maximum original tenor of one year

payload.correct_explanation_md: Temporary allocation is only in Level 1 HQLA with a maximum original tenure of one year.

payload.stem_md: How often is the allocation of green deposit proceeds subject to independent third-party verification or assurance?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The allocation in a financial year is subject to annual independent third-party verification or assurance.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is excluded from eligible green activities?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Hydropower plants larger than 25 MW are among the exclusions, with fossil fuel projects, nuclear power and landfills.

payload.stem_md: Within what time after the end of the financial year is the review report placed before the Board or its delegated committee?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The review report is placed within three months of the end of the financial year.

payload.stem_md: On what basis are green deposit proceeds to be allocated?

options.text_md: Only to the bank's own subsidiaries
Any project the borrower calls green
The official Indian green taxonomy (with interim categories until it is finalised)

payload.correct_explanation_md: Allocation is based on the official Indian green taxonomy; pending its finalisation, on the interim list of categories.

unresolved: The Directions are titled as covering climate finance and the management of climate change risks, but the copy read contains only the green deposits framework; no Reserve Bank provisions on assessing, managing or disclosing physical and transition risk were found or read, so the lesson on those risks rests on the courseware alone (a general description of the risks).

The Directions copy read is marked updated as on 1 October 2026, after the cut-off; the change noted (board committee wording) does not affect the facts used. The Indian green taxonomy had not been finalised in the text read.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
